screens.prompt: In B6, total the three costs, add 8% markup, and round the result to 2 decimals.

require.message: The total is summed before it is rounded: wrap the range in SUM.

hints.syntax: =ROUND(SUM(B2:B4)*1.08,2): the calculation first, then the decimals to keep.
hints.func-round: The number is 4450.3992 and the answer wants two decimals, so ROUND needs both arguments.
hints.func-sum: Add the three costs with SUM instead of typing 4120.74 into the formula.
hints.require-ref: Point at B2:B4, so a changed cost changes the total.
hints.value: 4120.74 times 1.08 is 4450.3992, and two decimals round that to 4450.4. An 8% markup is 1.08, not 1.8.
hints.error: A total of 4120.74 means the sum was rounded before the markup went on.

docs.explain:
ROUND takes a number and a count of decimals to keep. The three costs total 4120.74, and an 8% markup multiplies that by 1.08, which gives 4450.3992. Wrapping the whole calculation, =ROUND(SUM(B2:B4)*1.08,2), stores 4450.4.

ROUND changes the number itself. Showing 4450.3992 with two decimals leaves every digit in the cell, so the next column still adds 4450.3992. The stored 4450.4 is what the invoice carries, and 4450.40 on screen is that value with a format applied.

Put ROUND around the finished calculation. Rounding each cost after markup and then adding can land on a different figure from rounding the total, and this formula rounds once, at the end. A negative count rounds left of the point: -2 turns 4450.3992 into 4500.

errors.text: The second argument is text, such as "2" in quotes after a paste from another system.
The name is typed ROUNDOF or ROUND_UP, and Excel recognises only ROUND.
Rounding each cost after the markup and then adding gives a different sum from rounding the total once.

docs.atWork: Quotes and invoices, where the number on the page has to match the number the cell stores.
docs.outcome: Round a marked-up total once, and know that the stored value changed.

seo.title: ROUND in Excel: money to two decimals
seo.description: ROUND changes the stored value, formatting only changes what you see. A 4120.74 total with 8% markup stores 4450.3992 and rounds to 4450.4.
